result.topic_en: For rational x = h/m, the page studies the periodic function (nx) (the signed remainder of nh mod m), shows that the series of (nx)/n splits into convergent paired terms, and uses Abel summation via partial sums α_n to rewrite Σ(nx)/n.
result.transcription:
$x = \frac{h}{m}$ ; $m$ eine positive ganze Zahl
$n = n'm + n''$ ; $\frac{nh}{m} = h(n' + \frac{n''}{m}) = hn' + \frac{hn''}{m}$
$n'' = 0, 1 .. (m-1)$.
$h = k_1 m + h_1$
$2h = k_2 m + h_2$
$nh = k_n m + h_n$ wo $-\frac{m}{2} < h_n \leqq \frac{m}{2}$
$((n+m)x) = (nx)$
Ist $m$ ungerade, so ist $-\frac{m-1}{2} \leqq h_n \leqq \frac{m-1}{2}$ ; 0 kann wegfallen [?] | $n \equiv 0$
Ist $m$ gerade, so ist nur $-(\frac{m}{2}-1) \leqq h_n \leqq \frac{m}{2} - 1$ ; $n \equiv 0$ und $n \equiv \frac{m}{2}$ fallen aus
Es kommen daher Reihen zu [?] betrachten [?]
$\frac{1}{[-m-]n_1} - \frac{1}{n_2} + \frac{1}{n_1+m} - \frac{1}{n_2+m} + \frac{1}{n_1+2m} - \frac{1}{n_2+2m}$
$\frac{1}{n_1+tm} - \frac{1}{n_2+tm} = \frac{n_2-n_1}{n_1n_2 + (n_1+n_2)mt + m^2t^2}$ convergent.
$\sum_1^m (nx) = 0$ ; $\sum_1^n (nx) = \alpha_n$ ; $(nx) = \alpha_n - \alpha_{n-1}$ ; $\alpha_0 = 0$
$\sum_1^n \frac{(nx)}{n} = \sum_1^n \frac{\alpha_n - \alpha_{n-1}}{n} = \sum_1^n \frac{\alpha_n}{n} - \sum_1^n \frac{\alpha_{n-1}}{n} = \sum_1^n \frac{\alpha_n}{n} - \sum_0^{n-1} \frac{\alpha_n}{n+1}$
$= \sum_1^n \alpha_n (\frac{1}{n} - \frac{1}{n+1}) + \frac{\alpha_n}{n+1}$
$\sum_1^\infty \frac{(nx)}{n} = \sum_1^\infty \alpha_n (\frac{1}{n} - \frac{1}{n+1})$
